gen_risks.description: Legacy data inconsistencies may cause inaccurate enrolment and false exclusions in the NPR.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct comprehensive data cleaning, validation and biometric deduplication before enrolment; institute ongoing quality‑control checks.
gen_risks.evidence: existing databases had inconsistent quality and data formats, including Arabic and Latin alphabets, likely leading to substantial inaccuracies and processing requirements.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient ICT infrastructure in remote civil‑registry offices could delay enrolment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide backup power, satellite links, and a maintenance schedule; pre‑position spare equipment for isolated sites.
gen_risks.evidence: some of the 2,200 Civil Registry Offices are in very isolated areas and require substantial investments in overall infrastructure, beyond new hardware and software.

gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strong encryption, regular security audits, and staff training; monitor compliance with Law 09‑08.
gen_risks.evidence: MoI adopted a privacy‑by‑design approach to guarantee data privacy and protection.

gen_risks.description: End‑to‑end Error, Fraud and Corruption (EFC) monitoring system may be ineffective.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage experienced anti‑fraud vendor, pilot the EFC system, and refine based on monitoring results.
gen_risks.evidence: design and development of an end‑to‑end Error, Fraud, and Corruption (EFC) monitoring system and mitigation strategy to reduce its rate.

gen_risks.description: Transition of NPR/SR management to the newly created NRA may stall.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop a detailed hand‑over plan, recruit NRA staff early, and provide capacity‑building workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: Implementation of the NPR and the SR will be managed by the DIST … until the NRA is operational.

gen_risks.description: Use of Excel for IFRs may affect financial reporting quality and timeliness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt dedicated financial management software, automate IFR generation, and train FM staff.
gen_risks.evidence: use of a spreadsheet ‘Excel’ … may lead to challenges in quality and timeliness of IFRs and annual financial statements.

gen_risks.description: Duplication or overlap of budget lines (e.g., AMO‑TADAMON) could cause reporting errors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict budget‑coding procedures and cross‑check with World Bank templates.
gen_risks.evidence: risk of duplication or overlap due to the use of the same budget line ‘AMO‑TADAMON’ to justify expenditure.

gen_risks.description: Retroactive financing limited to 12‑month‑old expenditures may create cash‑flow gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain a cash‑flow buffer and align expenditures with eligible‑expenditure windows.
gen_risks.evidence: Retroactive financing may only be provided … for eligible expenditures incurred not more than 12 months before signing.

gen_risks.description: Delay in NRA operationalisation and staff recruitment (PBC‑linked).
gen_risks.mitigation: Set monthly milestone tracking, recruit key staff early, and conduct regular IMSC reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: PBCs target NRA operationalisation and staff recruitment by FY26 (see Table 2).

gen_risks.description: NPR coverage target (≥60 % of population) may be missed on schedule.
gen_risks.mitigation: Intensify enrolment campaigns, monitor weekly enrolment numbers, and deploy additional mobile units as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: The NPR national rollout strategy aims to expand coverage to more than 60 percent of the total population by end of 2024.

gen_risks.description: Informal‑sector workers may avoid enrolment fearing tax implications.
gen_risks.mitigation: Tailor outreach, assure no tax penalties, and simplify enrolment procedures for informal workers.
gen_risks.evidence: workers in the informal sector are wary of providing their information … due to perceived risks of making them susceptible to taxation.

gen_risks.description: Vulnerable groups could be excluded due to inadequate communication and outreach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy multi‑channel communication (TV, radio, SMS, community agents) and conduct feedback loops to improve awareness.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential negative social impacts … mainly related to the exclusion of some vulnerable groups due to inefficient or inadequate public communication and outreach efforts.

gen_risks.description: Amendments to Law 72‑18 or its decrees could disrupt implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a legal‑monitoring unit and maintain dialogue with the Ministry of Justice to anticipate changes.
gen_risks.evidence: Law no. 72‑18 and the three implementing decrees provide a solid legal and institutional framework.

gen_risks.description: Changes to data‑protection law (Law 09‑08) may create compliance gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Periodically review Law 09‑08 and update privacy‑by‑design controls accordingly.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will follow national regulations related to personal data protection (Law 09‑08).

gen_risks.description: Improper disposal of e‑waste from mobile units and equipment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt certified e‑waste recycling procedures and include disposal clauses in procurement contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: Risks associated with the use of electronic devices (such as mobile units) include the potential generation of e‑waste and its improper disposal.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related shocks (drought, floods) may increase demand for social protection.
gen_risks.mitigation: Build flexible targeting algorithms and reserve contingency funds for emergency response to climate events.
gen_risks.evidence: Morocco has undergone several overlapping shocks … climate change … droughts … represent significant risks to the Moroccan economy.

gen_risks.description: Economic recession from COVID‑19 could affect fiscal space and beneficiary ability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Diversify financing sources and maintain a contingency reserve within the loan to absorb fiscal shocks.
gen_risks.evidence: The COVID‑19 pandemic led to the first recession in over two decades due to reduced economic activity.

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risk is assessed as Substantial. Given the complex nature of the operation and the involvement of multiple stakeholders in the implementation of the National Population Register (NPR) and the Social Registry (SR), the Project Management Unit (PMU) will need to put considerable effort into ensuring better coordination to achieve the PDO. The national rollout and the improvement of the NPR and the SR will need strong stakeholder engagement, including citizens concerned by social protection programs who are often poor and vulnerable.
gt_risks.mitigation: The communication strategy will continue to inform all stakeholders involved in project implementation and will capitalize on lessons learned from the first Identity and Targeting for Social Protection project (P155198). The PMU envisions improving the grievance mechanism at local and national levels and establishing a system to promote citizen engagement and transparency. The Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee is responsible for developing guidelines for the strategic policy for the envisaged reform and ensuring a link with the ongoing social protection reform. Technical work will also cover a process evaluation to identify challenges, propose remedies, and provide recommendations to enhance system implementation at central and local levels.
